edges.description: Both concern rational/integer points on algebraic varieties; K3 surface lattice structure directly connects to lattice point counting
Brauer-Manin obstruction on K3 surface governs whether EC-based search can succeed
Sieve conditions mod p are exactly the local conditions that CRT would combine
CSP solution landscape is the fitness landscape; phase transition in CSP density maps to landscape ruggedness
A spectral gap in near-miss scores would be the analytic manifestation of an algebraic obstruction
Commensurate frequencies map to lattice points; resonance cavities define the geometric search space
Modular constraints act as arc-consistency propagation in the CSP formulation
Multi-objective optimization surface IS the fitness landscape in residual space
CRT succeeds iff there is no Brauer-Manin obstruction; failure of Hasse principle = CRT failure at the global level
Spectral gap in number theory is analogous to forbidden frequency bands in resonators

bridge_chains.insight: If modular sieves never completely exclude a candidate, CRT suggests local-global compatibility, but the Brauer-Manin obstruction could still block. This chain motivates computing the Brauer group of the cuboid K3 surface.
If near-misses show a widening gap (spectral gap), this is empirical evidence for a topological obstruction. Analyzing near-miss distributions can inform whether non-existence is provable.
CSP propagation + modular sieving + CRT reconstruction forms a complete algorithmic pipeline: reduce via constraints, sieve via local conditions, attempt global assembly.
